conviction_note: The cause is a completed flow event, not information: SCTX fell 15% intraday on the exact session the Russell quarterly IPO additions went effective at the open, while every gene-editing peer and both biotech indices rose, with no SEC filing since 2026-09-02, no press release and no analyst action. The forward calendar inside the window is empty on every line the second-shoe checklist covers, so the findings sum to +2.9; I cut that to +1.8 because this name's 14-day ATR of 12.1% is very high and high-ATR names keep falling (the best free ranker, rho=-0.126), because the cross-sectional prior for its bands is -0.295%, because its own comparable-fall history is only n=2, and because an 8-K covering a 2026-09-21 event could still land by 2026-09-25.
bar: The forward pipeline inside the window is empty. No SEC filing of any kind since the 2026-09-02 10-Q and Item 2.02 8-K (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001853921.json); Q3 results are due November; the only registered trial, STX-1150, has a primary completion of 2028-12-30 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07428473); the next company appearance is the Cell & Gene Meeting on the Mesa on 2026-10-05 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/01/3354090/0/en/scribe-therapeutics-to-participate-in-upcoming-investor-conferences.html); there is no options market, so there is no skew to price an event against.

cause.label: index_or_flow
cause.what_happened: SCTX fell 15.00% close-to-close on 2026-09-21 with essentially the whole move intraday (the open was only 0.36% below the prior close) on 2.75x normal volume, on the session FTSE Russell's September quarterly IPO additions became effective at the open, after a +10.96% five-day run-up into that date, and with no company filing, no press release, no analyst action and every gene-editing peer up on the day.

evidence.claim: FTSE Russell's September 2026 quarterly IPO additions were effective at the open of trading on 2026-09-21; preliminary lists were published 2026-08-21 covering 36 tickers, and SCTX appears on the Russell 2000 list, described as listing 2026-07-24 at $15/share with a concurrent Sanofi private placement.

Independent confirmation of the same mechanism and the same effective date: Evolution Metals & Technologies joined the Russell 3000 and Russell 2000 through FTSE Russell's Q3 2026 quarterly IPO additions effective 2026-09-21.

The fall was idiosyncratic, not sector or sympathy: on 2026-09-21 XBI +0.96%, IBB +1.27%, CRSP +3.13%, BEAM +1.24%, NTLA +0.66%, EDIT +4.81%, all measured from adjusted daily closes, while SCTX fell 15.00%.
The issuer has made no SEC filing of any kind since 2026-09-02, so no 8-K, no Item 4.02 non-reliance, no registration statement and no Form 144 accompanied the fall.
The issuer's own newsroom carries no headline between the 2026-09-02 Q2 results release and 2026-09-22, so no company announcement accompanied the fall.

pipeline.next_dated_event: Cell & Gene Meeting on the Mesa presentation by CFO David Parrot, 2026-10-05 — fourteen days outside the window. Nothing at all is dated inside it.
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: An 8-K landing on 2026-09-22 disclosing a 2026-09-21 event — the four-business-day clock for anything that happened on the drop day runs to 2026-09-25, so an information cause I could not see is still formally possible.

positioning_check: Short interest was 778,191 shares at the 08/31/2026 FINRA settlement, days to cover 2.63, up 173.3% from 284,711 shares at the 08/14/2026 settlement (https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/SCTX/short-interest?assetclass=stocks). FINRA settles twice monthly and publishes about eight business days later, so the position carried INTO the 2026-09-21 fall is not observable and the next settlement covering mid-September publishes around 2026-09-24, outside the window. Days to cover of 2.63 is not crowded enough to force a squeeze. Insiders show 11 open-market buys and 0 sells over both 3 and 12 months (https://api.nasdaq.com/api/company/SCTX/insider-trades). Float is the binding fact: approximately 17,577,400 shares were outstanding after the IPO and concurrent private placement (the 424B4 states 1% of shares outstanding equals approximately 175,774 shares), and substantially all non-IPO holders are locked up until 2027-01-19, leaving a tradeable float near the 8.6m IPO shares — which is why the 14-day ATR is 12.1%. There is no skew to read: the baseline records no_options_market.

findings.finding: The index demand that this stock ran up into is complete and dated — FTSE Russell's September quarterly IPO addition became effective at the open of 2026-09-21, so the 2026-09-22 session is the first with no index-related buying or front-running flow scheduled against it, and the pre-positioned sellers who drove the 15% intraday decline have no further index event to sell into.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This stock has fallen at or below -10.5% twice since its 2026-07-24 listing — -11.47% on 2026-08-13 and -16.21% on 2026-08-25 — and rose the next close both times, +1.77% and +1.57%, median +1.67%, up-rate 100% on n=2 (sealed baseline history block).
findings.why_not_priced: The price has taken the unwind of a flow event as though it were the disclosure of an adverse fact. If the market held the flow explanation, a 15% single-session decline would not have happened on a day when XBI, IBB and all four gene-editing comparables rose and the issuer had filed nothing for nineteen days; the fall would have been a normal post-add drift of a few percent. What the price has not taken is that the selling pressure has a known end date that has already passed.
findings.independence: The effective date and the mechanism are corroborated independently of the aggregator by an issuer press release for another company added in the same review: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/21/3365486/0/en/evolution-metals-technologies-corp-joins-russell-3000-and-russell-2000-indexes-gaining-exposure-to-12-2-trillion-in-benchmarked-assets.html

findings.finding: No analyst cut can land in the window: all four covering analysts initiated on 2026-08-18 at Buy or Overweight with price targets of $37, $50 and $60 against a $28.05 close, none has changed a rating or a target since, and no analyst action accompanied the 2026-09-21 fall — so the 'estimate cuts have only started' pattern that drives most continuation does not apply to this name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No analyst downgrade has ever landed on this stock — it has been public for two months and the only rating events on record are the 2026-08-18 initiations and a Zacks Research move to hold on 2026-09-01, neither of which coincided with either prior double-digit fall.
findings.why_not_priced: A 15% fall in a covered small-cap normally front-runs a sell-side revision. Here there is nothing to revise — no company news has been released since 2026-09-02 for an analyst to cut on. If the price held this, the decline would not have been concentrated in one session with the sell-side untouched on either side of it.
findings.independence: The quiet-period initiation cluster is separately visible in the 2026-09-03 weekly ratings roundup: https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/09/03/scribe-therapeutics-sctx-investment-analysts-weekly-ratings-updates.html

findings.finding: No dilution or supply mechanism can act in the window: the filing record contains zero mentions of 'at-the-market' ever, the company is not S-3 shelf-eligible until roughly July 2027, the IPO lock-up runs to 2027-01-19, and the 2026-09-02 release states $43.0m of cash at 30 June plus approximately $140.6m of net IPO and private-placement proceeds funds operations into the first half of 2029 — so the going-concern language that appeared in the pre-IPO S-1 and 424B4 has no route back into a filing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no history of a supply event on this stock: it has been listed for two months, has filed one S-8 for its own equity plans and no resale or shelf registration, and the sealed baseline's full-text probes return 0 hits ever for 'at-the-market', 'minimum bid price' and 'non-reliance'.
findings.why_not_priced: The commonest second leg down after a fall of this size in a small-cap biotech is an opportunistic raise or an ATM drawn into the bounce, and at $28.05 against a $15.00 IPO price this company would be an obvious candidate. It structurally cannot do it inside this window. If the price held that, the fall would not have been steeper than either of this name's two prior double-digit declines, both of which happened when the same balance sheet was in place.
findings.independence: The absence of an ATM and of any non-reliance or bid-price item is independently established from the SEC's own full-text search, recorded in the sealed baseline's text_probes block against https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001853921.json

baseline_tension: It agrees with the volume and with this name's own history — 2.75x is at the benign end of the base-rate table, where under 2x pays +1.46% against -2.44% above 15x, and both of this stock's prior comparable falls bounced (+1.77%, +1.57%, median +1.67%) — but it cuts hard against the free ranker, because a 14-day ATR of 12.1% is very high and high-ATR names keep falling (rho=-0.126, family-wise p=0.0017), and against the cross-sectional prior for its drop-size and turnover bands, which is -0.295%; so expected_move_pct is set at +1.8 against a findings sum of +2.9, a cut of 1.1 points.
